Pangrams, by number of letters.Mr Jock, TV quiz PhD…: 'Mr Jock, TV quiz PhD, bags few lemons' is a 26-letter pangram, meaning it uses each letter of the alphabet just once.
Pangrams, by number of letters.Waltz, bad nymph…: 'Waltz, bad nymph, for quick jigs vex' uses all 26 letters with only a couple of extras.
Pangrams, by number of letters.Sphinx of black quartz…: 'Sphinx of black quartz, judge my vow' is a favorite for testing typefaces, and it is a short sentence with all letters.
Pangrams, by number of letters.How vexingly quick…: 'How vexingly quick daft zebras jump!' is a fun sentence that uses all 26 letters.
Pangrams, by number of letters.Jackdaws love my big sphinx…: 'Jackdaws love my big sphinx of quartz' is a classic test for typists.
Pangrams, by number of letters.Pack my box with five…: 'Pack my box with five dozen liquor jugs' is a commonly used pangram, and it was used to test typewriters.
Pangrams, by number of letters.The quick brown fox…: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' is the best-known pangram, used to test typewriters and fonts since the 1800s.
Pangrams, by number of letters.Amazingly few discotheques…: 'Amazingly few discotheques provide jukeboxes' is a well-known pangram, and it uses a lot of repeated letters.
Pangrams, by number of letters.Crazy Fredrick bought…: 'Crazy Fredrick bought many very exquisite opal jewels' is a pangram, and it contains a couple of repeated letters.
Pangrams, by number of letters.We promptly judged antique…: 'We promptly judged antique ivory buckles for the next prize' is a long pangram that uses 26 letters with plenty of repeats.

Westerns by release.Stagecoach: John Ford's film made John Wayne a star, and it was shot in Monument Valley.
Westerns by release.High Noon: It plays out in nearly real time, with Gary Cooper watching the clock.
Westerns by release.Shane: It features a boy's cry, Shane! Come back!, one of the most quoted movie endings.
Westerns by release.The Searchers: Its famous final shot through a doorway influenced directors such as Scorsese and Spielberg.
Westerns by release.The Magnificent Seven: It is a remake of Kurosawa's Seven Samurai.
Westerns by release.The Good, the Bad and the Ugly: Sergio Leone directed it, and Ennio Morricone's score is iconic.
Westerns by release.Butch Cassidy: It won four Oscars, and the Sundance Kid inspired the name of Robert Redford's festival.
Westerns by release.Dances with Wolves: It won Best Picture, and much of the dialogue is in Lakota with subtitles.
Westerns by release.Unforgiven: Clint Eastwood directed it and won Oscars for Best Picture and Best Director.
Westerns by release.True Grit (Coen brothers): Based on Charles Portis's novel, it earned an Oscar nomination for 14-year-old Hailee Steinfeld.

Materials by density.Air: A cubic metre of air at sea level weighs about 1.2 kg, so the air in a living room can outweigh a grown person.
Materials by density.Cork: Cork is mostly gas-filled cells, and it is harvested from cork oak bark roughly every nine years without killing the tree.
Materials by density.Pine wood: Most woods float because they are less dense than water, though balsa, at around 160, is far lighter than pine.
Materials by density.Ice: Water expands by about 9% as it freezes, which is why ice floats; lakes freeze from the top down and fish survive underneath.
Materials by density.Water: The kilogram was first defined as the mass of a litre of water, which is why water's density is such a tidy 1,000.
Materials by density.Concrete: Concrete is the most widely used man-made material, and humans consume more of it than any substance except water.
Materials by density.Aluminium: About a third as dense as steel, it suits aircraft and cans; it was once so costly that Napoleon III reportedly served on aluminium plates.
Materials by density.Steel: Steel is mostly iron with a little carbon, and it is among the most recycled materials on Earth.
Materials by density.Lead: Its Latin name plumbum gives us the symbol Pb and the word plumber, because Romans piped water through lead.
Materials by density.Gold: All the gold ever mined would fit into a cube only about 22 metres on each side, thanks to its extreme density.

Numbers in hex, binary and octal.0b101: The 0b prefix marks binary, where only 0 and 1 exist, because computers are built from on-off switches.
Numbers in hex, binary and octal.0xA: Hex uses the letters A to F for 10 to 15, which is why web colours look like #FF0000.
Numbers in hex, binary and octal.0o17: Octal groups bits in threes, and Unix file permissions like 755 are written this way.
Numbers in hex, binary and octal.0x10: In hex, sixteen is written 10, just as ten is in decimal, hence the joke about 10 types of people.
Numbers in hex, binary and octal.0b11001: In binary it's 16 + 8 + 1, with each place being double the one to its right.
Numbers in hex, binary and octal.0x2A: This is 42, the Hitchhiker's Guide answer, and a fitting one: in the ASCII character set 0x2A happens to be the asterisk.
Numbers in hex, binary and octal.0o100: It equals 64, a power of two and the number of squares on a chess board, written as 100 just as hundred is in decimal.
Numbers in hex, binary and octal.0x64: In the ASCII character table, 0x64 is the lowercase letter d, so a stream of text can hide a lot of hex.
Numbers in hex, binary and octal.0b11111111: The largest value a byte can hold is also the highest value each RGB colour channel can take.
Numbers in hex, binary and octal.0xBEEF: Hex 'words' like BEEF, DEAD and CAFE are programmers' jokes, and 0xDEADBEEF is a classic placeholder.

Spy movies by release.Dr. No: The first Bond film starred Sean Connery, and Ursula Andress's emergence from the sea became iconic.
Spy movies by release.The Ipcress File: Michael Caine played the bespectacled Harry Palmer, a deliberately unglamorous answer to Bond.
Spy movies by release.Three Days of the Condor: Robert Redford stars in this CIA conspiracy thriller, based on the novel Six Days of the Condor.
Spy movies by release.Austin Powers: Mike Myers's parody of 1960s spy films gave us Dr. Evil, shagadelic catchphrases, and sequels that outgrossed the first.
Spy movies by release.Spy Kids: Robert Rodriguez's family film about child spies, in which two kids rescue their agent parents, led to three sequels.
Spy movies by release.The Bourne Identity: It's based on Robert Ludlum's novel, and Matt Damon's casting launched a franchise.
Spy movies by release.Johnny English: Rowan Atkinson's bumbling spy began in a series of Barclaycard ads, before the character got his own movie.
Spy movies by release.Mr. & Mrs. Smith: Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie met on the set of this action comedy, and went on to become one of Hollywood's best-known couples.
Spy movies by release.Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy: Based on John le Carré's novel, he was himself a former British intelligence officer, and Gary Oldman played Smiley.
Spy movies by release.Kingsman: The Secret Service: Colin Firth stars in this adaptation of a comic by Mark Millar and Dave Gibbons.

Boiling points of liquids and molten stu.Diethyl ether: It was an early anaesthetic in the 1840s, and boils just above body temperature, so it evaporates fast.
Boiling points of liquids and molten stu.Acetone: A solvent used in nail polish remover, it is also made in the body during ketosis.
Boiling points of liquids and molten stu.Ethanol: Distillation works because ethanol boils below water, which concentrates spirits.
Boiling points of liquids and molten stu.Water: At altitude water boils at lower temperatures; on top of Everest it boils at only about 70 °C, hardly enough for tea.
Boiling points of liquids and molten stu.Glycerol: Its high boiling point suits food and cosmetics uses, and it is also what makes e-cigarette vapour from the liquid.
Boiling points of liquids and molten stu.Mercury: The only metal liquid at room temperature, it has been used in thermometers, though it has been phased out for toxicity.
Boiling points of liquids and molten stu.Sulfur: Sulfur burns with an eerie blue flame, and it is the 'brimstone' of the Bible, from an old word for 'burning stone'.
Boiling points of liquids and molten stu.Sodium: Sodium vapour lamps give old streetlights their orange glow, because excited sodium atoms emit a strong yellow-orange light.
Boiling points of liquids and molten stu.Iron: Iron melts at 1,538 °C, and it is gaseous only at extreme temperatures like those in stars.
Boiling points of liquids and molten stu.Tungsten: It has the highest boiling point of any metal, and is used in light-bulb filaments.

When these famous events were first held.Kentucky Derby: Run at Churchill Downs on the first Saturday in May, it is nicknamed the Run for the Roses and covers 1.25 miles.
When these famous events were first held.Wimbledon: The oldest tennis tournament, famous for its strict all-white dress code for players.
When these famous events were first held.Stanley Cup: Named for Lord Stanley, Canada's Governor General, who donated it, and the names of winners are engraved on the trophy.
When these famous events were first held.Boston Marathon: Inspired by the 1896 Olympic marathon, it is held on Patriots' Day each April.
When these famous events were first held.Rose Bowl Game: The first game, in 1902, saw Michigan beat Stanford 49 to 0, so one-sided the game was dropped until 1916.
When these famous events were first held.Tour de France: Created by a newspaper, L'Auto, to boost sales. The yellow jersey echoes the paper's yellow pages.
When these famous events were first held.Indianapolis 500: Winners drink milk, a tradition that started in 1936.
When these famous events were first held.Ryder Cup: Named for Samuel Ryder, a seed merchant who donated the trophy for the competition between Europe and the US.
When these famous events were first held.FIFA World Cup: It was held in Uruguay, which won it, with only 13 teams taking part.
When these famous events were first held.The Masters: It is played at Augusta National each year, and the winner is awarded a green jacket.

In the US, the age when you can first....Open a social media account: The age comes from a 1998 US privacy law for children, COPPA, and is about collecting data, not about maturity.
In the US, the age when you can first....Drive (most states): Most states use graduated licenses, which restrict night driving and teen passengers during the first year.
In the US, the age when you can first....Vote: The 26th Amendment in 1971 lowered the voting age to 18 amid the Vietnam War, under the slogan old enough to fight, old enough to vote.
In the US, the age when you can first....Buy alcohol: The National Minimum Drinking Age Act of 1984 pushed every state to set 21 by threatening to withhold highway funds.
In the US, the age when you can first....Serve in the US House: The Constitution sets 25 as the minimum age for House members, plus seven years of citizenship, so it is easy to hit.
In the US, the age when you can first....Serve in the US Senate: The Senate requires age 30 and nine years of citizenship, set higher than the House to suggest more maturity.
In the US, the age when you can first....Become US President: You must be 35, a natural-born citizen, and a resident for 14 years, and John F. Kennedy was the youngest elected, at 43.
In the US, the age when you can first....Join AARP: The group's name was formerly the American Association of Retired Persons, but it dropped the long title in 1999.
In the US, the age when you can first....Get Medicare: Medicare was created in 1965, and Harry Truman, who had urged it for years, received the first Medicare card.
In the US, the age when you can first....Get full Social Security: Social Security began with a retirement age of 65 in 1935, and it has been raised gradually to 67 for people born in 1960 or later.

The American Revolution, in order.Stamp Act: It taxed paper goods and inspired the slogan No taxation without representation, before being repealed in 1766.
The American Revolution, in order.Boston Massacre: Five colonists died; Crispus Attucks, of African and Native descent, is often called the first, and John Adams defended the soldiers.
The American Revolution, in order.Boston Tea Party: Colonists dumped 342 chests of East India Company tea into the harbor, and some were disguised as Mohawks.
The American Revolution, in order.Lexington and Concord: Called the shot heard round the world, it began on April 19, the day Paul Revere made his ride.
The American Revolution, in order.Declaration of Independence: Jefferson wrote it, and John Adams expected July 2, the day independence was voted, to be the holiday, not July 4.
The American Revolution, in order.Battle of Saratoga: Seen as the turning point, it convinced France to ally with the Americans, with Benedict Arnold's heroics central.
The American Revolution, in order.Siege of Yorktown: Cornwallis surrendered after the French navy blocked his escape, in the last major land battle.
The American Revolution, in order.Treaty of Paris: Britain recognized American independence and a western border at the Mississippi River.
The American Revolution, in order.Constitution signed: Thirty-nine delegates signed in Philadelphia, and Franklin said he had seen that the sun carved on the chair was rising.
The American Revolution, in order.Washington inaugurated: He took the oath in New York City, then the capital, at Federal Hall, after a unanimous vote of the electors.

C operator precedence.Function call: Postfix operators like function calls, array brackets and member access share the top level and group left to right.
C operator precedence.Logical NOT: Unary operators such as ! and ~ sit just below postfix ones and group right to left.
C operator precedence.Multiplication: It binds tighter than addition, so 1 + 2 * 3 gives 7, the same rule as school arithmetic.
C operator precedence.Addition: Addition and subtraction share a level and group left to right, so 10 - 3 - 2 is 5, not 9.
C operator precedence.Bit shift: Shifts rank below addition, so 1 << 2 + 1 means 1 << 3, a classic surprise for programmers.
C operator precedence.Less-than comparison: Relational operators sit above equality, so a < b == c < d compares two true-or-false results.
C operator precedence.Equality comparison: A classic C bug: a & b == c parses as a & (b == c), because equality binds tighter than bitwise AND.
C operator precedence.Bitwise AND: It ranks beneath comparisons, which is why people parenthesize flag tests like (x & MASK) == 0.
C operator precedence.Logical OR: Both && and || short-circuit and run left to right, and && binds tighter than ||.
C operator precedence.Assignment: Assignment binds nearly loosest and groups right to left, so a = b = c works as a = (b = c).

When these great fires burned.Great Fire of Meireki (Edo): The 1657 fire destroyed much of Edo and killed an estimated 100,000 people, and the castle keep was never rebuilt.
When these great fires burned.Great Fire of London: It began in a Pudding Lane bakery and destroyed about 13,000 houses and St Paul's Cathedral.
When these great fires burned.Fire of Moscow: Fires raged after Napoleon's army occupied the city, and many blame Russians for setting them.
When these great fires burned.Great Fire of Hamburg: It burned for around four days, destroying a large part of the city center, and rebuilding modernized the city.
When these great fires burned.Great Chicago Fire: Legend blames Mrs O'Leary's cow; the fire killed about 300 and left 100,000 homeless.
When these great fires burned.San Francisco quake fire: Most of the destruction was from fires, not the quake, and broken water mains left firefighters helpless.
When these great fires burned.Triangle Shirtwaist fire: A garment factory fire in New York killed 146 workers behind locked exits and spurred US workplace safety laws.
When these great fires burned.Reichstag fire: The fire in Berlin let the Nazis suspend civil liberties by decree, and its cause is still debated.
When these great fires burned.Hindenburg disaster: The airship burst into flames at Lakehurst, New Jersey, killing 36; reporter Herbert Morrison's radio account made it unforgettable.
When these great fires burned.Windsor Castle fire: It broke out in the Queen's 'annus horribilis' of 1992, and restoration took about five years.

World War II, in order.Germany invades Poland: The German invasion of Poland in September 1939 triggered Britain and France declaring war.
World War II, in order.Dunkirk evacuation: Hundreds of small boats, from fishing vessels to pleasure craft, helped rescue more than 300,000 Allied troops from France.
World War II, in order.Operation Barbarossa: Germany's invasion of the Soviet Union was the largest in history, involving millions of troops.
World War II, in order.Pearl Harbor: The surprise attack on the US naval base in Hawaii pulled America into the war the next day.
World War II, in order.Battle of Midway: US carriers sank four Japanese carriers here, and it is regarded as the turning point of the Pacific war.
World War II, in order.Germans surrender Stalingrad: Voyager 1 is the farthest human-made object, and it entered interstellar space in 2012.
World War II, in order.D-Day: The Allies landed on beaches in Normandy, and it was the largest seaborne invasion in history.
World War II, in order.Battle of the Bulge: Germany's last big offensive in the west happened in freezing Ardennes forests, and it left a bulge in the Allied line.
World War II, in order.VE Day: The day Germany's surrender was celebrated in Europe, and crowds filled the streets of London.
World War II, in order.Hiroshima: The US dropped the first atomic bomb on this Japanese city, and Japan surrendered days later.

Food inventions, oldest to newest.Bird's baking powder: Alfred Bird, a British chemist, made it; he also invented eggless custard for his allergic wife.
Food inventions, oldest to newest.Pasteurization: Louis Pasteur first worked on it to stop wine and beer spoiling, not milk.
Food inventions, oldest to newest.Margarine: Hippolyte Mege-Mouriès made it after Napoleon III called for a cheap butter substitute; the original used beef fat.
Food inventions, oldest to newest.Heinz ketchup: Early ketchups were fish sauces from Southeast Asia; the sweet tomato version came much later.
Food inventions, oldest to newest.Coca-Cola: Atlanta pharmacist John Pemberton created it, and it was first sold at a soda fountain for five cents a glass.
Food inventions, oldest to newest.Corn flakes: The Kellogg brothers accidentally made flakes at a Michigan sanitarium after leaving cooked wheat sitting out.
Food inventions, oldest to newest.Birdseye quick-frozen food: Clarence Birdseye was inspired by seeing Inuit in Labrador freeze fish quickly in the Arctic air.
Food inventions, oldest to newest.Nescafé instant coffee: Nestle developed it to help Brazil use its huge coffee surplus.
Food inventions, oldest to newest.Swanson TV dinner: Swanson reportedly had a huge surplus of leftover Thanksgiving turkey, and put it on trays with sides to sell.
Food inventions, oldest to newest.Pringles: The saddle-shaped chips are made from dough, not whole potatoes, and stack neatly in a tube.

When these mathematicians were born.Pythagoras: His followers formed a cult; the theorem bearing his name was known in Babylon long before him.
When these mathematicians were born.Archimedes: He supposedly shouted 'Eureka!' in the bath, and was killed by a Roman soldier when Syracuse fell in 212 BC.
When these mathematicians were born.Hypatia: An Alexandrian mathematician and astronomer, she was killed by a mob in 415.
When these mathematicians were born.Al-Khwarizmi: His name gave us the word 'algorithm', and his book al-jabr gave us 'algebra'.
When these mathematicians were born.Fibonacci: He brought Hindu-Arabic numerals to Europe in Liber Abaci; his rabbit puzzle gave us his famous sequence.
When these mathematicians were born.René Descartes: He gave us Cartesian coordinates, and 'I think, therefore I am'.
When these mathematicians were born.Isaac Newton: His Principia of 1687 laid out the laws of motion and gravity; he later ran the Royal Mint.
When these mathematicians were born.Leonhard Euler: The most prolific of mathematicians, he kept working after going blind, and gave us the notation e and i.
When these mathematicians were born.Carl Friedrich Gauss: Legend says as a child he quickly summed 1 to 100; he was called the 'Prince of Mathematicians'.
When these mathematicians were born.Srinivasa Ramanujan: A self-taught Indian genius who wrote to G. H. Hardy; Hardy's taxi number, 1729, became famous because of him.

When these poets and playwrights were bo.Sappho: The poet from Lesbos wrote songs of love and longing, but only one complete poem and fragments of the rest survive.
When these poets and playwrights were bo.Aeschylus: Called the father of tragedy, he added a second actor. A legend says he died when an eagle dropped a tortoise on his head.
When these poets and playwrights were bo.Sophocles: He wrote over 100 plays, but only seven survive complete, among them Oedipus the King and Antigone.
When these poets and playwrights were bo.Aristophanes: The great comic playwright of Athens mocked politicians and philosophers, and even Socrates in The Clouds.
When these poets and playwrights were bo.Menander: Most of his comedies were lost for centuries, until papyri found in Egypt in the 20th century brought back a near-complete play.
When these poets and playwrights were bo.Virgil: He wrote the Aeneid, and reportedly asked for it to be burned on his deathbed, but Emperor Augustus had it saved.
When these poets and playwrights were bo.Ovid: Author of Metamorphoses, he was banished by Augustus to a remote Black Sea town in 8 AD, for reasons never fully explained.
When these poets and playwrights were bo.Juvenal: The satirist is the source of the phrase 'bread and circuses', a jab at citizens who care only for food and entertainment.
When these poets and playwrights were bo.Li Bai: A Tang dynasty poet famed for his love of wine and the moon. A legend says he drowned trying to embrace the moon's reflection.
When these poets and playwrights were bo.Murasaki Shikibu: A court lady in Heian Japan, she wrote The Tale of Genji, often called the world's first novel.

Tiny things by size.Proton: Nobody has seen inside one, since a proton is made of three quarks held together by the strong force.
Tiny things by size.Uranium nucleus: Though it holds 238 particles, the nucleus is about 10,000 times smaller than the atom around it.
Tiny things by size.Hydrogen atom: Hydrogen is the simplest atom and makes up about three quarters of all ordinary matter by mass.
Tiny things by size.DNA double helix width: Stretched out, the DNA in a single human cell would be about two metres long.
Tiny things by size.Flu virus: Flu viruses change so quickly that vaccines must be updated almost every year.
Tiny things by size.Wavelength of green light: Our eyes are most sensitive near this colour, which is why night-vision gear and safety vests lean green or yellow.
Tiny things by size.E. coli bacterium: Most strains of this gut bacterium are harmless, and under good conditions it can divide every 20 minutes.
Tiny things by size.Red blood cell: They have no nucleus, and your body makes about two million new ones every second.
Tiny things by size.Human hair width: Hair grows about a centimetre a month, and its width varies widely between people.
Tiny things by size.Grain of sand: Geologists define sand by size, from about 0.06 to 2 mm, regardless of what mineral it is made of.

Korean (Sino-Korean) numbers, by value.il: Sino-Korean numbers like this are used for dates, money and minutes, while native Korean numbers count objects.
Korean (Sino-Korean) numbers, by value.i: The same syllable, written 이, also means tooth and this in Korean.
Korean (Sino-Korean) numbers, by value.sam: It appears in samgyeopsal, three-layered pork belly, a staple of Korean barbecue.
Korean (Sino-Korean) numbers, by value.sa: Many buildings skip a fourth floor because it sounds like the word for death.
Korean (Sino-Korean) numbers, by value.o: It appears in obangsaek, the traditional five directional colours of Korean art.
Korean (Sino-Korean) numbers, by value.yuk: The Korean War is called Yuk-i-o, 6-2-5, after the date of 25 June 1950 when it began.
Korean (Sino-Korean) numbers, by value.chil: The seventh day of the seventh lunar month is Chilseok, a festival of star-crossed lovers.
Korean (Sino-Korean) numbers, by value.pal: Pal-do means the eight provinces, as Joseon-era Korea was divided into eight regions.
Korean (Sino-Korean) numbers, by value.gu: The nine-tailed fox of Korean folklore is called gumiho.
Korean (Sino-Korean) numbers, by value.baek: Baek-il, the 100th day of a baby's life, is celebrated with rice cakes.

Bears, and animals called bears.Water bear (tardigrade): Microscopic 'water bears' can survive the vacuum of space, intense radiation and decades of drying out.
Bears, and animals called bears.Woolly bear caterpillar: Folklore says the width of its stripes predicts winter severity, but it doesn't.
Bears, and animals called bears.Red cat-bear (red panda): In Chinese its name means 'little bear cat'; it belongs to its own family, not the giant panda's.
Bears, and animals called bears.Koala (not a bear): It is a marsupial, and it sleeps up to 20 hours a day on a eucalyptus diet.
Bears, and animals called bears.Bearcat (binturong): Its smell is often compared to buttered popcorn, and it has a prehensile tail.
Bears, and animals called bears.Sun bear: The smallest bear has a long tongue for reaching honey and a golden crescent on its chest.
Bears, and animals called bears.Antbear (aardvark): Its name is Afrikaans for 'earth pig', and it can eat tens of thousands of termites a night.
Bears, and animals called bears.American black bear: Despite the name, it can be cinnamon-colored, and it is the most common bear in North America.
Bears, and animals called bears.Grizzly bear: Named for its silver-tipped 'grizzled' fur, it can sprint at over 50 km/h.
Bears, and animals called bears.Polar bear: The largest land carnivore has black skin under hollow, transparent fur.

Superhero team movies by release.Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: A low-budget film that became one of the highest-grossing independent movies of its time.
Superhero team movies by release.X-Men: Hugh Jackman got Wolverine late, after the original actor, Dougray Scott, dropped out.
Superhero team movies by release.The Incredibles: Pixar's family of supers, directed by Brad Bird, won the Oscar for Best Animated Feature.
Superhero team movies by release.Fantastic Four (Story): Marvel's first family debuted in comics in 1961, launching the Silver Age of Marvel. This film starred Jessica Alba.
Superhero team movies by release.The Avengers: It brought Iron Man, Captain America, Thor and the Hulk together and earned over $1.5 billion.
Superhero team movies by release.Guardians of the Galaxy: Marvel took an obscure comic and made a hit, with a talking tree and an old-music mixtape soundtrack.
Superhero team movies by release.Suicide Squad: Margot Robbie played Harley Quinn, and the film won an Oscar for makeup and hairstyling.
Superhero team movies by release.Justice League: After Snyder left the original, a director's cut came out in 2021 following a long fan campaign.
Superhero team movies by release.Eternals: Directed by Chloe Zhao, who had just won the Best Director Oscar for Nomadland.
Superhero team movies by release.Thunderbolts*: A Marvel team of antiheroes. The asterisk in its title is part of the branding.

From blood to bladder: how urine is made.Afferent arteriole: Blood arrives here at the kidney's filter. The kidneys receive about a fifth of the heart's output.
From blood to bladder: how urine is made.Glomerulus: A tangle of capillaries whose name means 'little ball'. Together your kidneys filter about 180 litres a day.
From blood to bladder: how urine is made.Bowman's capsule: A cup-shaped structure named after English surgeon William Bowman.
From blood to bladder: how urine is made.Proximal tubule: It reabsorbs most of the water, glucose and salts that were filtered, which is why you do not pee away your sugar.
From blood to bladder: how urine is made.Loop of Henle: A hairpin-shaped section that builds a salty gradient, letting the kidney make concentrated urine.
From blood to bladder: how urine is made.Distal tubule: Fine-tunes salt and acid balance under the control of hormones like aldosterone.
From blood to bladder: how urine is made.Collecting duct: Hormones such as ADH decide here how much water to save, which sets how dilute your urine ends up.
From blood to bladder: how urine is made.Renal pelvis: A funnel-shaped chamber that gathers urine before sending it down the ureter.
From blood to bladder: how urine is made.Ureter: A muscular tube about 25 centimetres long that pushes urine along with waves of squeezing, not just gravity.
From blood to bladder: how urine is made.Bladder: It can hold around half a litre, though the urge to go typically begins well before it is full.

Seeds and pits, from dust to giant.Orchid seed: Orchid seeds are dust-like with almost no food reserves, so in nature they depend on a partner fungus to germinate.
Seeds and pits, from dust to giant.Poppy seed: A single poppy capsule holds thousands of seeds, and buried ones can stay dormant in the soil for many years until the ground is disturbed.
Seeds and pits, from dust to giant.Sesame seed: Sesame is one of the oldest oil crops, and its ripe pods pop open with a snap, a likely inspiration for "open sesame".
Seeds and pits, from dust to giant.Apple seed: Plant an apple seed and you almost never get the parent's fruit; that is why orchards graft cuttings instead of sowing seeds.
Seeds and pits, from dust to giant.Cherry pit: The kernel inside a cherry pit contains amygdalin, which can release cyanide when crushed and eaten in quantity, so nobody should chew them.
Seeds and pits, from dust to giant.Date pit: Date palms have been farmed for thousands of years, and the hard pits were ground into animal feed or roasted as a coffee substitute.
Seeds and pits, from dust to giant.Peach pit: A peach is a close relative of the almond, and inside its woody, wrinkled stone sits a kernel that looks like a small almond.
Seeds and pits, from dust to giant.Avocado pit: Growing an avocado from its pit is a classic home experiment, yet orchards graft instead, because pit-grown trees take years and vary in fruit.
Seeds and pits, from dust to giant.Coconut: The coconut is a seed built for ocean travel: its buoyant husk can drift for months on currents and plant palms on far tropical shores.
Seeds and pits, from dust to giant.Coco de mer: Native to two Seychelles islands, this is the heaviest seed in the world, weighing up to about 20 kg, and its odd shape fed old legends.

Tech toys by release.Speak & Spell: The Speak and Spell used one of the first single-chip speech synthesizers, and a version of it appeared in E.T. as the alien's communicator.
Tech toys by release.Teddy Ruxpin: Teddy Ruxpin was a talking bear that moved its mouth and eyes while playing tapes, and it was a huge hit in the mid-1980s.
Tech toys by release.Talkboy: Talkboy was a tape recorder featured in Home Alone 2, and the film's success made the real toy a must-have.
Tech toys by release.Tamagotchi: Tamagotchi were handheld virtual pets that needed feeding and cleaning, and they were so popular that schools banned them.
Tech toys by release.Furby: Furby could 'learn' English, and the NSA reportedly banned them from its offices over fears they could record secrets.
Tech toys by release.Sony AIBO: Sony's AIBO was an early robot dog, and it could learn tricks and show emotions with LED eyes.
Tech toys by release.Webkinz: Webkinz toys came with a code to unlock a virtual pet online, and they were a hit among kids in the 2000s.
Tech toys by release.Skylanders: Skylanders was the first game to use toy figures that you place on a portal to bring characters into a video game.
Tech toys by release.Hatchimals: Hatchimals are toys that hatch from eggs, and they sold out wildly in the 2016 holiday season.
Tech toys by release.Nintendo Labo: Nintendo Labo uses cardboard kits you fold and combine with Switch controllers to make things like a piano or fishing rod.

Courses of a classic French dinner, in o.Apéritif: A light drink before the meal, such as a kir or pastis, meant to open the appetite; the word comes from the Latin for 'to open'.
Courses of a classic French dinner, in o.Amuse-bouche: The name means 'mouth amuser', and it is a small free bite sent out by the chef rather than ordered from the menu.
Courses of a classic French dinner, in o.Soup (potage): The word 'potage' shares its root with the English 'pottage', a thick stew cooked in a pot.
Courses of a classic French dinner, in o.Fish course: It comes before the meat because courses are traditionally ordered from lightest to heaviest.
Courses of a classic French dinner, in o.Sorbet palate cleanser: In Normandy a similar pause is called the trou normand, when a shot of Calvados is taken mid-meal.
Courses of a classic French dinner, in o.Main course: The 'plat principal' is the centrepiece, but in classic French service it often appears with only a modest vegetable.
Courses of a classic French dinner, in o.Salad: In France the salad usually comes after the main course, supposedly to help digestion.
Courses of a classic French dinner, in o.Cheese: France makes well over 1,000 cheeses, and Charles de Gaulle is often quoted asking how to govern a nation with so many.
Courses of a classic French dinner, in o.Dessert: The word comes from the French 'desservir', meaning to clear the table.
Courses of a classic French dinner, in o.Digestif: Brandy such as Cognac or Armagnac is traditionally served in small amounts in the belief that it settles the stomach.

How heavy is a typical adult?.House mouse: Its front teeth never stop growing, so it must constantly gnaw to keep them worn down.
How heavy is a typical adult?.Golden hamster: All pet golden hamsters descend from a single mother and her litter found in Syria in 1930.
How heavy is a typical adult?.Guinea pig: The name 'cavy' is more accurate; like humans, guinea pigs can't make their own vitamin C.
How heavy is a typical adult?.House cat: A house cat sleeps about 12 to 16 hours a day, a leftover from its life as an ambush hunter.
How heavy is a typical adult?.Beaver: The second-largest rodent has orange teeth thanks to iron in the enamel, and a flat tail used as a rudder.
How heavy is a typical adult?.Gray wolf: Every domestic dog is descended from it, though dogs split from their wolf ancestors thousands of years ago.
How heavy is a typical adult?.Lion: Unusually for a cat, lions live in groups called prides, and a male's roar can be heard from kilometres away.
How heavy is a typical adult?.Horse: A horse can sleep standing, thanks to a system of tendons that locks the legs in place.
How heavy is a typical adult?.Hippopotamus: Despite its bulk, its closest living relatives are whales and dolphins, not pigs.
How heavy is a typical adult?.African elephant: This is the largest land animal, and it can eat well over 100 kg of plants in a single day.

Fitness crazes, by when they took off.Pilates's New York studio: Joseph Pilates called his method Contrology, and he developed it while interned in England in the First World War.
Fitness crazes, by when they took off.Bowerman's book Jogging: Nike's co-founder Bill Bowerman's book helped spark America's jogging boom, and he later poured rubber into a waffle iron to make soles.
Fitness crazes, by when they took off.Cooper's book Aerobics: Air Force doctor Kenneth Cooper coined the term and argued that steady exercise protects the heart.
Fitness crazes, by when they took off.Jane Fonda's Workout: Her VHS tape was a huge bestseller and helped start the home-video market.
Fitness crazes, by when they took off.ThighMaster: The infomercial gadget, pitched by Suzanne Somers, became a pop culture joke.
Fitness crazes, by when they took off.Tae Bo: Billy Blanks's martial arts and aerobics mix was a hit on videotape, and the name is short for taekwondo and boxing.
Fitness crazes, by when they took off.CrossFit: Greg Glassman's high-intensity regimen began in a small California gym and grew into a global chain.
Fitness crazes, by when they took off.P90X: Tony Horton's 90-day home video program was marketed by its 'muscle confusion'.
Fitness crazes, by when they took off.Shake Weight: The dumbbell's shaking motion, promoted in infomercials, was widely mocked.
Fitness crazes, by when they took off.Peloton bike: The stationary bike with live streamed classes began as a crowdfunded startup in New York.

Women writers, by birth year.Murasaki Shikibu: A court lady in Heian Japan, she wrote The Tale of Genji around 1000 AD, often called the world's first novel.
Women writers, by birth year.Mary Shelley: She conceived Frankenstein at 18 during a gloomy summer by Lake Geneva, when Lord Byron proposed a ghost-story contest.
Women writers, by birth year.Charlotte Brontë: She published Jane Eyre in 1847 as Currer Bell; she and her sisters hid behind male-sounding pen names.
Women writers, by birth year.George Eliot: Mary Ann Evans chose a male pen name to be taken seriously, and Middlemarch is often ranked among the greatest English novels.
Women writers, by birth year.Louisa May Alcott: Little Women drew on her own family of four sisters, and she wrote it at her publisher's request, though she preferred thrillers.
Women writers, by birth year.Edith Wharton: She was the first woman to win the Pulitzer Prize for fiction, in 1921 for The Age of Innocence.
Women writers, by birth year.Agatha Christie: Often ranked the best-selling novelist ever, with an estimated two billion copies; her play The Mousetrap has run in London since 1952.
Women writers, by birth year.Harper Lee: To Kill a Mockingbird won a Pulitzer, and she published nothing else until Go Set a Watchman appeared in 2015.
Women writers, by birth year.Margaret Atwood: She has said everything in The Handmaid's Tale had historical precedent, and she has won the Booker Prize twice.
Women writers, by birth year.Zadie Smith: Her debut White Teeth came out in 2000 when she was in her mid-twenties and made her an overnight literary star.

An embryo's first two months, in order.Fertilization: Sperm and egg meet, usually in the fallopian tube, forming a single cell with 46 chromosomes.
An embryo's first two months, in order.First cell division: The cell divides about a day after fertilization, but cleavage splits the cell without growing, so the pieces get smaller.
An embryo's first two months, in order.Four-cell stage: Each cell is still totipotent, able in principle to become a whole person, which is how identical twins can arise.
An embryo's first two months, in order.Morula: The name is Latin for mulberry, since this solid ball of cells looks like one.
An embryo's first two months, in order.Blastocyst: A hollow ball with an inner cell mass that becomes the embryo and an outer layer that helps form the placenta.
An embryo's first two months, in order.Implantation begins: The blastocyst burrows into the uterine lining, and the pregnancy hormone hCG that tests detect begins here.
An embryo's first two months, in order.Gastrulation: The embryo forms three layers, which become skin and nerves, muscle and bone, and gut; biologist Lewis Wolpert called it the most important time in your life.
An embryo's first two months, in order.Heart starts beating: A simple tube starts pulsing, often before the mother knows she's pregnant.
An embryo's first two months, in order.Neural tube closes: The tube that becomes brain and spinal cord seals shut; folic acid helps prevent failures like spina bifida.
An embryo's first two months, in order.Fetal period begins: The major organ systems have been started, and from here the baby mostly grows and matures.

Fonts by year of design.Futura: Paul Renner built it from circles, triangles and squares; it was used on the plaque left on the Moon by Apollo 11.
Fonts by year of design.Times New Roman: The Times of London commissioned it for its newspaper, and Stanley Morison and Victor Lardent designed it.
Fonts by year of design.Courier: Howard Kettler designed it at IBM for typewriters, where every letter takes the same width; it remains the screenwriter's standard.
Fonts by year of design.Helvetica: Swiss designer Max Miedinger created it as Neue Haas Grotesk, and it earned its own documentary in 2007.
Fonts by year of design.Arial: Designed as a cheaper look-alike for Helvetica, with the same character widths, so documents wouldn't reflow.
Fonts by year of design.Wingdings: A font made of pictures instead of letters; its name echoes dingbats, the printers' ornaments it modernizes.
Fonts by year of design.Comic Sans: Vincent Connare designed it for speech balloons in a Microsoft program, and its infamy hasn't stopped some dyslexic readers from liking it.
Fonts by year of design.Verdana: Matthew Carter designed it for small, legible text on screens, with wide letters and generous spacing.
Fonts by year of design.Calibri: It replaced Times New Roman as Microsoft Word's default in 2007, and held that role for 16 years.
Fonts by year of design.Aptos: Calibri's successor as Microsoft's default; it was first called Bierstadt, after a Colorado mountain.

Quirky units of volume.Minim: An old apothecary unit roughly equal to a single drop of water, with 60 minims making a fluid dram.
Quirky units of volume.Teaspoon (US): The US teaspoon is about 4.9 ml, while medicine is measured as a rounded 5 ml, so kitchen spoons are not true measuring tools.
Quirky units of volume.Tablespoon (US): A US tablespoon is three teaspoons, but in Australia it's 20 ml, so recipes can swing by a third across the Pacific.
Quirky units of volume.Jigger: The double-sided bartender's cup holds about 1.5 US ounces, the standard single shot in many American bars.
Quirky units of volume.Cup (US): A US cup is about 237 ml, but Australia, Canada and New Zealand use a rounder 250 ml in recipes.
Quirky units of volume.Gallon (US): The US gallon, from the old English wine gallon, is smaller than the imperial gallon, which is about 4.55 liters.
Quirky units of volume.Firkin (of beer): A quarter barrel, named from a Middle Dutch word for fourth, holding nine imperial gallons of beer.
Quirky units of volume.Oil barrel: Holds 42 US gallons by tradition, and nowadays oil is rarely moved in actual barrels, yet prices are still quoted per barrel.
Quirky units of volume.Hogshead: A cask of about 63 gallons used for wine, beer and whisky; the name may come from a Dutch word for hog's head.
Quirky units of volume.Tun: A huge cask of 252 gallons, whose name gave us tonnage, since ships were once rated by the tuns of wine they could carry.

Famous ad campaigns, by debut year.The Marlboro Man: It was launched to give filter cigarettes a rugged image; some of the actors who played the cowboy later died of smoking-related illness.
Famous ad campaigns, by debut year.Coke's Hilltop ad: The 'I'd Like to Buy the World a Coke' ad was shot on an Italian hillside with hundreds of young people, and the song became a hit single.
Famous ad campaigns, by debut year.Mean Joe Greene Coke ad: The Steelers star tosses his jersey to a young fan for a Coke; the spot became so beloved it inspired a TV movie.
Famous ad campaigns, by debut year.Apple's Big Brother Mac ad: Ridley Scott directed this Macintosh launch spot, which aired nationally only once, during the Super Bowl, yet became legendary.
Famous ad campaigns, by debut year.Budweiser's Whassup?: It grew from a short film by Charles Stone III in which his real friends greeted each other this way; parodies followed everywhere.
Famous ad campaigns, by debut year.Dove Campaign for Real Beauty: It used everyday women instead of professional models, and the debate it sparked about beauty standards spread worldwide.
Famous ad campaigns, by debut year.Most Interesting Man in World: Actor Jonathan Goldsmith was in his late sixties when he won the role, and 'Stay thirsty, my friends' became a catchphrase.
Famous ad campaigns, by debut year.Compare the Meerkat: Aleksandr Orlov, a Russian-accented meerkat, was dreamed up for a price comparison site and spawned a catchphrase, 'Simples!'.
Famous ad campaigns, by debut year.Old Spice: The Man Your Man: Isaiah Mustafa, towel-clad, delivered the pitch in one continuous take, and the team then answered fans online with personalised videos.
Famous ad campaigns, by debut year.Share a Coke: The bottles swapped the logo for popular first names; the idea began in Australia and spread to dozens of countries.

When these leaders were assassinated.Abraham Lincoln: Shot by John Wilkes Booth at Ford's Theatre on 14 April 1865, days after the Civil War effectively ended. He died the next morning.
When these leaders were assassinated.Tsar Alexander II: The tsar freed the serfs in 1861. Revolutionaries killed him with a bomb in St Petersburg, and a church was built on the spot.
When these leaders were assassinated.Archduke Franz Ferdinand: His death in Sarajevo at the hands of Gavrilo Princip set off a chain of alliances. A month later, Europe was at war.
When these leaders were assassinated.Leon Trotsky: Exiled by Stalin, he was killed with an ice axe in Mexico City. His killer, Ramón Mercader, served 20 years in prison.
When these leaders were assassinated.Mahatma Gandhi: Gandhi was shot at a prayer meeting in Delhi, just months after India's independence. His funeral drew millions.
When these leaders were assassinated.John F. Kennedy: He was shot in Dallas on 22 November, while riding in an open car. Many people recall where they were when they heard.
King was shot at the Lorraine Motel in Memphis, the day after his "I've been to the mountaintop" speech. He was 39.
When these leaders were assassinated.Anwar Sadat: Egypt's president, who signed a peace treaty with Israel, was shot by soldiers during a military parade. He had shared a Nobel Peace Prize.
When these leaders were assassinated.Indira Gandhi: India's prime minister was killed by her own bodyguards. She was the only woman to lead India, and the daughter of Nehru.
When these leaders were assassinated.Yitzhak Rabin: Israel's prime minister was shot after a peace rally in Tel Aviv. He had won a Nobel Peace Prize a year earlier.

Climate swings of the past, in order.Younger Dryas cold snap: A sudden return to near-ice-age cold, lasting around 1,200 years, just as the last glaciation seemed to be ending.
Climate swings of the past, in order.8.2-kiloyear cooling: Probably triggered when a giant glacial lake drained into the North Atlantic, cooling the Northern Hemisphere for a century or two.
Climate swings of the past, in order.Roman Warm Period: During this warm spell across Europe, Romans planted vineyards as far north as Britain.
Climate swings of the past, in order.Medieval Warm Period: Vikings settled Greenland during this warmth, and farms there were abandoned after the cold returned.
Climate swings of the past, in order.Maunder Minimum begins: A 70-year shortage of sunspots, named for astronomer Edward Maunder, coincided with the coldest stretch of the Little Ice Age.
Climate swings of the past, in order.Europe's Great Frost: In the winter of 1709, rivers such as the Seine froze solid and famine killed hundreds of thousands in France.
Climate swings of the past, in order.Laki haze: Iceland's Laki eruption spewed toxic gases and killed around a fifth of the island's people, while cooling parts of Europe.
Climate swings of the past, in order.The Year Without a Summer: After Tambora erupted in 1815, snow fell in New England in June; the gloom inspired Mary Shelley's Frankenstein.
Climate swings of the past, in order.Dust Bowl peak: Drought and over-plowed prairies fed 'black blizzards'; in May 1934 a huge storm dropped Great Plains soil on New York and Washington.
Climate swings of the past, in order.Britain's Great Storm: Hurricane-force winds felled about 15 million trees in southern England in one night, after a forecast that denied a hurricane.

From pumpkin seed to jack-o'-lantern.Plant seeds in spring: Pumpkins are planted after the last frost, since seeds will not sprout in cold soil. They need a long growing season of about three to four months.
From pumpkin seed to jack-o'-lantern.Vines spread out: The sprawling vines can grow several metres, with large leaves and tiny hairs. Tendrils help them cling and spread across the garden.
From pumpkin seed to jack-o'-lantern.Yellow flowers open: Pumpkins make separate male and female flowers on the same plant. The blooms last only one day, and they are edible and used in cooking.
From pumpkin seed to jack-o'-lantern.Bees pollinate them: Bees carry pollen from male to female flowers. Without pollination, the female blossoms shrivel and no pumpkin forms.
From pumpkin seed to jack-o'-lantern.Little green pumpkin forms: The baby fruit appears at the base of the female flower. It swells quickly, and can gain a kilo or more a day for the biggest varieties.
From pumpkin seed to jack-o'-lantern.Pumpkin turns orange: As the fruit ripens, the green chlorophyll breaks down and the orange carotenoids are revealed. These are the same pigments found in carrots.
From pumpkin seed to jack-o'-lantern.Harvest in autumn: Pumpkins are harvested before the first hard frost, and cut with a bit of stem left on. A tough rind shows that they are ripe.
From pumpkin seed to jack-o'-lantern.Scoop out the seeds: The seeds can be roasted for a snack. Pumpkin seeds, called pepitas, are rich in minerals like magnesium and zinc.
From pumpkin seed to jack-o'-lantern.Carve a spooky face: The tradition came from Ireland, where people carved turnips and beets for Halloween. Immigrants to America switched to pumpkins, which were bigger and easier to carve.
From pumpkin seed to jack-o'-lantern.Light a candle inside: The jack-o'-lantern is named after Stingy Jack, a figure from Irish folklore who was doomed to wander with a coal inside a carved turnip.

Mathematicians, by birth year.Pythagoras: The Greek philosopher led a secretive brotherhood that held numbers sacred; his famous theorem was already known to the Babylonians centuries earlier.
Mathematicians, by birth year.Euclid: His Elements was a standard geometry textbook for over two thousand years, yet almost nothing is known about his life.
Mathematicians, by birth year.Al-Khwarizmi: A scholar in Baghdad's House of Wisdom, his name gave us the word algorithm, and his book Al-Jabr gave us algebra.
Mathematicians, by birth year.Fibonacci: Leonardo of Pisa helped popularise Hindu-Arabic numerals in Europe; the sequence bearing his name began as a rabbit-breeding puzzle.
Mathematicians, by birth year.René Descartes: He linked algebra and geometry with coordinates, which is why we call the x-y grid the Cartesian plane, and wrote I think, therefore I am.
Mathematicians, by birth year.Isaac Newton: He developed calculus and the law of gravitation, and later spent years as Warden and Master of the Royal Mint chasing counterfeiters.
Mathematicians, by birth year.Leonhard Euler: The most prolific mathematician in history, he kept producing work after going blind, and popularised the symbols e, i and pi.
Mathematicians, by birth year.Carl Friedrich Gauss: As a child he is said to have summed the numbers 1 to 100 within seconds; he was later called the prince of mathematicians.
Mathematicians, by birth year.Ada Lovelace: Lord Byron's daughter wrote what is seen as the first computer program, for Babbage's Analytical Engine, a century before computers existed.
Mathematicians, by birth year.Alan Turing: He helped break Enigma messages at Bletchley Park and defined what a computer can compute; computing's top prize is named after him.

Christmas traditions, by when they began.Dec 25 observed in Rome: The earliest record of Christmas on December 25 in Rome dates from the time of Emperor Constantine, who legalised Christianity.
Christmas traditions, by when they began.Strasbourg Christmas tree: A document from Strasbourg mentions fir trees decorated with apples, paper roses and sweets, the earliest known reference to Christmas trees.
Christmas traditions, by when they began.Boston bans Christmas: Puritans thought Christmas was unbiblical and fined anyone caught celebrating, a law that stayed until 1681.
Christmas traditions, by when they began.Night Before Christmas: The poem, first published anonymously, shaped Santa's image with sleigh and reindeer; it is usually credited to Clement Clarke Moore, though that is debated.
Christmas traditions, by when they began.First Christmas card: Henry Cole commissioned it in London and sold about a thousand copies; some people frowned at the picture of a child drinking wine.
Christmas traditions, by when they began.US federal holiday: President Grant signed the law, although at first the holiday applied only to federal workers in Washington, D.C.
Christmas traditions, by when they began.Rockefeller tree: Construction workers set up a small tree on the building site during the Depression, and the formal lighting tradition began soon after.
Christmas traditions, by when they began.Rudolph created: Robert L. May wrote the poem for Montgomery Ward's department stores, which gave away millions of copies in the first year.
Christmas traditions, by when they began.White Christmas song: Irving Berlin, a Jewish immigrant, wrote it, and Bing Crosby's recording is often called the best-selling single of all time.
Christmas traditions, by when they began.Home Alone: It earned over $450 million worldwide and made a generation of viewers re-watch it every December.

Chinese zodiac animals, in order.Rat: Legend says the Rat won the great race by riding on the Ox's back, then leaping ahead at the finish line.
Chinese zodiac animals, in order.Ox: It carried the rat across the river in the legend, and finished second; the ox symbolises diligence.
Chinese zodiac animals, in order.Tiger: The stripes on a tiger's forehead resemble the character for king, which is why it is called the king of beasts in China.
Chinese zodiac animals, in order.Rabbit: Vietnam's zodiac replaces the Rabbit with the Cat, while the Chinese Rabbit is tied to the moon rabbit myth.
Chinese zodiac animals, in order.Dragon: It is the only mythical creature in the zodiac, and birth rates tend to rise in Chinese communities in Dragon years.
Chinese zodiac animals, in order.Snake: In one version of the race, it hid on the horse's hoof and startled the horse at the finish.
Chinese zodiac animals, in order.Horse: 2026 is a Fire Horse year, a combination that only comes around every 60 years.
Chinese zodiac animals, in order.Goat: The same Chinese character covers goat, sheep and ram, so translations vary.
Chinese zodiac animals, in order.Monkey: Sun Wukong, the Monkey King of Journey to the West, is the most famous monkey in Chinese lore.
Chinese zodiac animals, in order.Rooster: It is the only bird in the zodiac, and its crowing at dawn made it a symbol of punctuality.

Famous books, by publication year.Don Quixote: Cervantes's novel is often called the first modern novel, and it gave English the word quixotic.
Famous books, by publication year.Robinson Crusoe: Defoe's book was loosely inspired by Alexander Selkirk, a real castaway, and it spawned a whole genre of Robinsonades.
Famous books, by publication year.Pride and Prejudice: Austen wrote its first draft in her early twenties as First Impressions, and its opening line is among the most famous in English.
Famous books, by publication year.Jane Eyre: It was published under the pen name Currer Bell, so readers wouldn't know Charlotte Bronte was a woman.
Famous books, by publication year.Moby-Dick: It sold poorly in Melville's lifetime, and only gained fame decades after his death in 1891.
Famous books, by publication year.Alice in Wonderland: Lewis Carroll, real name Charles Dodgson, first told the story on a boat trip for Alice Liddell and her sisters.
Famous books, by publication year.Dracula: Bram Stoker never visited Transylvania; he based his research on books and folklore.
Famous books, by publication year.The Hobbit: Tolkien reportedly scribbled its first line, In a hole in the ground there lived a hobbit, on a blank exam page while grading.
Famous books, by publication year.Nineteen Eighty-Four: Orwell wrote it on the remote Scottish island of Jura, and terms like Big Brother and doublethink come from it.
Famous books, by publication year.Harry Potter (first book): Twelve publishers rejected it before Bloomsbury accepted it, and the first print run was only about 500 copies.
